articles.title: Mayors to get powers to overrule local councils on planning decisions
articles.summary: Housing minister Matthew Pennycook said the change was "essential" for helping mayors "effectively deliver new homes".
articles.content:
Mayors across England will be given new powers to overrule local councils on some planning decisions.

The change would apply to proposals with more than 150 homes, more than 15,000 square metres of commercial space or buildings over 30 metres.

Mayors in 13 areas including Manchester, Liverpool, the West of England and the West Midlands will gain similar powers to Sir Sadiq Khan in London, who is already able to "call in" planning decisions.

Housing minister Matthew Pennycook said the powers were an "essential part of the toolkit that mayors need to effectively deliver new homes and regeneration".

The Conservatives questioned whether it was right for councils to lose the "ability to make planning decisions in their own communities".

The powers will also be available to mayors in the Combined Authorities in North East England, South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, York and North Yorkshire, Hull and East Yorkshire, Greater Lincolnshire, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, East Midlands, and Tees Valley.

Housebuilding has fallen in London in recent years, but Pennycook insisted the "call in" powers had helped the mayor "unblock strategic growth sites" in the capital.

In the 2024 general election, the Labour government promised to build 1.5 million homes in England by the end of the decade but housebuilders have warned the target could be missed.

Pennycook said the government was "absolutely determined to stick with that ambition".

He acknowledged the target was "really stretching" but said nearly 180,000 children were in temporary accommodation and "any smaller target wouldn't be commensurate with the scale of the challenge".

In addition to gaining the new "call-in" powers, mayors are set to be able to grant "up-front permission", which the government says will allow building to begin "without a developer having to apply".

A consultation on how the powers will work is due to be published next week.

The government has sought to stress that local councils will continue to decide the majority of applications and that all decisions must still follow planning rules.

It has also said mayors will get a "bigger say" over how housing funding is spent in their area, with the government directing national agency Homes England to focus on local mayors' priorities.

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who served as mayor for Greater Manchester for nearly a decade, has repeatedly expressed his desire to transfer more powers to local mayors.

"Challenge does need to be made to local decision-making and actually it cuts both ways," he told the Sunday Times.

"Sometimes it's the other way round. It's the local authority putting forward something that's unacceptable in terms of the impact on the community. It's a two-way street."

Last month, Burnham promised to give all mayors a share of income tax revenue, saying he wanted to "bring power home" to "every postcode".

Earlier this week, he announced a secondment programme to send high-performing civil servants to work in mayoral offices.

The approach has faced criticism from some in his own party and the Liberal Democrats, who fear it could create a "two-tier system" that discriminates against those areas that do not have an elected mayor.

articles.personality_title: Mayors in England gain new powers to speed up housing projects
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – In England, local councils usually decide on planning permission for new buildings. However, housing shortages have made it harder to build enough homes, especially affordable ones. To help solve this, the government is changing the rules.

**What happened** – The government announced that mayors in 13 major areas, including Manchester, Liverpool, and the West Midlands, will now have the power to overrule local councils on some big planning decisions. This applies to projects with over 150 homes, large commercial spaces, or tall buildings. London’s mayor, Sadiq Khan, already has this ability. The new powers also let mayors approve plans quickly, so building can start faster without waiting for developers to apply.

**Impact** – This change is important because it helps mayors push forward large housing projects that local councils might delay or block. It aims to increase the number of homes being built, which is crucial since many children live in temporary housing. Giving mayors more control also means they can better focus on local housing needs and regeneration, helping communities grow and improve.

**What's next step** – A consultation will be published soon to explain how these new powers will work in detail. Meanwhile, mayors will also get more say in how housing money is spent in their areas. The government plans to continue supporting the goal of building 1.5 million new homes in England by 2030.

**One-sentence takeaway** – New government rules will let mayors in England speed up big housing projects by overruling local councils, aiming to build more homes faster and improve communities.
articles.personality_title_fr: Les maires en Angleterre obtiennent de nouveaux pouvoirs pour accélérer les projets de logement
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – En Angleterre, ce sont généralement les conseils locaux qui décident des permis de construire. Mais la pénurie de logements rend difficile la construction de maisons, surtout abordables. Pour aider à résoudre ce problème, le gouvernement change les règles.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Le gouvernement a annoncé que les maires de 13 grandes régions, comme Manchester, Liverpool et les West Midlands, pourront désormais annuler certaines décisions des conseils locaux sur les grands projets. Cela concerne les projets de plus de 150 logements, les grands espaces commerciaux ou les bâtiments hauts. Le maire de Londres, Sadiq Khan, a déjà ce pouvoir. Les maires pourront aussi approuver rapidement les plans pour que la construction commence sans attendre les demandes des promoteurs.

**Impact** – Ce changement est important car il aide les maires à faire avancer rapidement de grands projets de logement que les conseils locaux pourraient retarder ou bloquer. Cela vise à augmenter le nombre de maisons construites, ce qui est essentiel car beaucoup d'enfants vivent dans des logements temporaires. Donner plus de contrôle aux maires leur permet aussi de mieux répondre aux besoins locaux et de régénérer les communautés.

**Prochaine étape** – Une consultation sera bientôt publiée pour expliquer en détail comment ces nouveaux pouvoirs fonctionneront. En même temps, les maires auront plus de pouvoir sur la façon dont l'argent du logement est dépensé dans leurs régions. Le gouvernement continue de soutenir l'objectif de construire 1,5 million de nouveaux logements en Angleterre d'ici 2030.

**Une phrase clé** – De nouvelles règles permettront aux maires d'Angleterre d'accélérer les grands projets de logement en annulant les décisions des conseils locaux, pour construire plus vite et améliorer les communautés.
articles.personality_title_es: Los alcaldes en Inglaterra obtienen nuevos poderes para acelerar proyectos de vivienda
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – En Inglaterra, normalmente los ayuntamientos deciden sobre los permisos para construir nuevas viviendas. Pero la falta de casas ha dificultado construir suficientes, especialmente las asequibles. Para ayudar, el gobierno está cambiando las reglas.

**Qué pasó** – El gobierno anunció que los alcaldes de 13 grandes zonas, como Manchester, Liverpool y West Midlands, podrán anular algunas decisiones de los ayuntamientos sobre proyectos grandes. Esto aplica a proyectos con más de 150 viviendas, grandes espacios comerciales o edificios altos. El alcalde de Londres, Sadiq Khan, ya tiene este poder. Los alcaldes también podrán dar permisos rápidos para que la construcción empiece sin esperar que los desarrolladores pidan permiso.

**Impacto** – Este cambio es importante porque ayuda a los alcaldes a avanzar en grandes proyectos de vivienda que los ayuntamientos podrían retrasar o bloquear. El objetivo es aumentar la construcción de casas, algo necesario ya que muchos niños viven en alojamientos temporales. Más control para los alcaldes también significa que pueden enfocarse mejor en las necesidades locales y mejorar las comunidades.

**Próximo paso** – Pronto se publicará una consulta para explicar cómo funcionarán estos nuevos poderes. Mientras tanto, los alcaldes tendrán más voz sobre cómo se gasta el dinero para viviendas en sus áreas. El gobierno sigue comprometido con la meta de construir 1.5 millones de casas nuevas en Inglaterra para 2030.

**Frase clave** – Nuevas reglas permitirán a los alcaldes en Inglaterra acelerar grandes proyectos de vivienda anulando decisiones de ayuntamientos, con el fin de construir más rápido y mejorar las comunidades.
